newsitem.title: USA: Texas mother possibly wounded by attacker - expert.
newsitem.headline: Texas mother possibly wounded by attacker - expert.

text.p: A forensic expert said on Tuesday that a Dallas mother accused of murdering her two young sons suffered knife wounds that appeared to have been inflicted by an attacker.

The defence testimony was aimed at defusing prosecution charges that Darlie Routier, 27, killed her sons with a knife and then stabbed herself to give credence to her story that an intruder committed the crimes.
Routier faces the death penalty if convicted of killing sons Devon, 6, and Damon, 5, on June 6 in their Dallas area home.
Bexar County chief medical examiner Vincent DiMaio testified that Routier had stab wounds on the back of her right forearm that would have been consistent with fending off an attacker.
Her wounds would have had to have been inflicted with her left hand, which would have been unusual since Routier is right-handed, DiMaio said.
"People who are right-handed will use their right hand, they don't think about it ... people don't do things the hard way, they do things simple," he told the jury.
Prosecutors charged that Routier killed the children because she was upset about her weight problem and the family's financial difficulties.
Husband Darin Routier testified on Tuesday his wife was asleep when an intruder broke into their house and stabbed the boys. He also denied he and Darlie had money problems.

Before Tuesday's testimony, state District Judge Mark Tolle ruled that defence attorneys could not ask further questions of police detective Jimmy Patterson, who admitted on the stand Monday that the boys' grave had been bugged.

Patterson said police placed a microphone at the grave to try to get evidence against Routier during a graveside service. Defence attorneys charged that the bugging was illegal, which prompted Patterson to plead Fifth Amendment protection to avoid incriminating himself. Tolle said the line of questioning was irrelevant to the case.
Defence attorneys said they could wrap up their case as early as Wednesday. The trial was moved to Kerrville, about 60 miles northwest of San Antonio, Texas, because of heavy pre-trial publicity.
